newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan Tamil rebels kill 15 security men.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan Tamil rebels kill 15 security men.

text.p: Tamil Tiger guerrillas killed at least 15 Sri Lankan home guards and policemen when they overran a remote police post at a northeastern village early on Sunday, military officials said.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels were believed to have captured arms and ammunition from the Wanela post, about 28 km (17 miles) from the northeastern port of Trincomalee, they said.

"The post was destroyed," said an official. "Twelve home guards and three police constables were killed." Several security men wounded in the attack by a large force of rebels were in serious condition, he added.
The attack came as the army advanced on the rebels' northern Kilinochchi stronghold, backed by tanks, artillery and aircraft.
The Defence Ministry has said some 1,500 rebels have been either killed or wounded while the army has lost 219 soldiers in the week-long offensive. Nearly 300 soldiers have been wounded.
The rebels have put up stiff resistance with heavy rocket- ropelled grenade and mortar fire and have tried to stall the army's advance with fierce counterattacks, defence officials said.
A military spokesman said the rebels had blown up a telecommunications tower in Kilinochchi "in desperation".
"Terrorists transmissions indicate that they are summoning the maximum number of their cadres to the Kilinochchi area to fight a last-ditch battle," he said.
The rebels are fighting for independence in the Indian Ocean island's north and east. The government has said more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year.
